finding.description: The per-picture slice counter is an unbounded int, while decoded macroblock ownership is stored in a uint16_t slice table initialized to 0xFFFF. On slice 65535, storing slice_num aliases the unused-entry sentinel. The picture initializer deliberately re-poisons the table's spare mb_stride column with that sentinel, so neighbor checks can treat padded entries as members of the current slice. With deblocking_filter == 2 at mb_x == 0, the false top-left match selects top_borders[top_idx][-1], one 96-byte macroblock record before the heap allocation, and the luma and chroma XCHG operations write through it. Later FFmpeg repair 6d57428858 rejects current_slice >= 0xFFFE before incrementing, independently confirming the exact collision boundary.
finding.code_snippet: sl->slice_num = ++h->current_slice;
finding.poc: Decode one H.264 picture containing at least 65535 accepted slices so slice_num becomes 0xFFFF, then reach a left-edge macroblock with deblocking_filter == 2 and a padded top-left slice-table entry; the sentinel collision enables the top_borders[-1] luma/chroma exchanges.

vulnerability_trace.summary: attacker-controlled slice count reaches a wider counter, truncates into the 16-bit ownership table as its 0xFFFF sentinel, and corrupts a neighbor-existence decision before luma and chroma exchanges through a pointer one 96-byte record before top_borders

steps.note: The 16-bit table uses 0xFFFF for unavailable/padded entries.
The active table has leading guard rows and an mb_stride equal to mb_width + 1, leaving a spare padding column.
Every frame re-poisons the active table, including the spare per-row column, with the colliding 0xFFFF sentinel.
No terminating bound prevents slice_num from reaching 65535.
The int counter is stored into the uint16_t table.
Six FMO/non-FMO comparisons use slice-table equality to decide whether top-left, top, left, and top-right neighbors exist; the collision reverses the intended unavailable-entry result.
Only the deblocking_filter == 2 branch consults the colliding entry; the alternative explicitly requires mb_x > 0.
At mb_x == 0 this forms a pointer one 96-byte top-border record before the allocation.
The falsely enabled luma exchange writes through the underflowed heap pointer; the 4:4:4 and non-4:4:4 chroma exchanges repeat the write at lines 573-574 and 586-587.

finding.description: The Vulkan HEVC start-frame path copies each current short- or long-term RPS list into a Vulkan StdVideoDecodeH265PictureInfo array whose API-defined capacity is 8. FFmpeg's parser and RPS builder allow an individual list to contain up to 15 short-term references or up to 16 retained references. Unlike the NVDEC path, the Vulkan path does not reject a list count above the destination capacity, so i >= 8 writes beyond RefPicSetStCurrBefore, RefPicSetStCurrAfter, or RefPicSetLtCurr into adjacent picture-info fields.

finding.poc: Use Vulkan HEVC decoding on a valid stream whose current short-term-before, short-term-after, or long-term RPS contains more than eight used references that resolve in the DPB.

vulnerability_trace.summary: bitstream RPS counts survive parser checks and RPS construction with more than eight members, then directly bound writes into three eight-entry Vulkan API arrays

finding.description: ff_rdt_parse_header skips leading RDT status packets while at least five bytes remain. It reads a packet-controlled 16-bit pkt_len and rejects only values greater than the remaining input. A zero length therefore passes validation, after which both buf and len are advanced by zero and the status-packet condition remains unchanged forever. A direct 16-byte header with the followed-by-data flag, status marker, and zero packet length deterministically consumes CPU until externally terminated.
finding.code_snippet: while (len >= 5 && buf[1] == 0xFF) { pkt_len = AV_RB16(buf + 3); if (pkt_len > len) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA; buf += pkt_len; len -= pkt_len; }

finding.description: The RDT AAC cache path copies every unconsumed byte of a received record into a fixed RTP_MAX_PACKET_LENGTH plus padding buffer without checking the remaining length. An AAC VBR packet declaring one cached subpacket consumes only its four-byte count and length table, then returns a positive cache count. A 9216-byte record therefore makes production rdt_parse_packet copy 9212 bytes into the 8256-byte payload buffer. The direct production-parser harness deterministically aborts under ASan on a heap-buffer-overflow write in that memcpy on both sealed snapshots.

Repeating the parser-valid value across 24 maximum-order MMR pieces also exceeds the generator's constant 177-byte-per-piece allocation estimate, after which the always-on flush assertion aborts. TensorFlow detection explicitly requires four output names, so its intended count writes the terminator into a fifth pointer slot. A production ff_dnn_init harness with four generic output names produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow before backend lookup or model loading on both snapshots.

finding.description: TensorFlow inference allocates and returns task->nb_output tensors, and the registered TensorFlow detection path requires four outputs. Cleanup attempts to derive that runtime count with sizeof(*output_tensors) divided by sizeof(output_tensors[0]); both operands describe one pointer, so the result is always one. Only the first TensorFlow output tensor is deleted before the pointer array is freed. Every processed detection frame therefore leaks three complete model output tensors, allowing sustained valid use to exhaust memory. The sealed builds omit TensorFlow, so this remains source-confirmed rather than dynamically reproduced.
finding.code_snippet: int nb_output = sizeof(*request->output_tensors)/sizeof(request->output_tensors[0]); for (i = 0; i < nb_output; ++i) TF_DeleteTensor(...);
finding.poc: Configure vf_dnn_detect with its required four-output TensorFlow model and process frames while monitoring output-tensor allocations; three of four tensors per request are not passed to TF_DeleteTensor.

finding.description: The NellyMoser encoder's optional trellis search caps idx_max with OPT_SIZE but rejects a candidate only when idx is greater than that inclusive cap. An exactly-OPT_SIZE transition therefore indexes one element beyond a trellis row. Those transitions are reachable from ordinary audio samples, and repeated row-edge writes can corrupt the following row; at the final band the corresponding read crosses the end of the complete allocation. A short public white-noise encode with volume 10 and trellis enabled produces UBSan reports for opt and path at index 35768 followed by an ASan heap-buffer-overflow read exactly after the 3,290,656-byte opt allocation on both sealed snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: idx_max = FFMIN(OPT_SIZE, cand[band - 1] + q); ... if (idx > idx_max) break; ... opt[band][idx]

finding.description: The RTP/AV1 depacketizer intentionally discards temporal-delimiter and tile-list OBUs, but that branch advances the output packet cursor and remaining input length without advancing the input cursor. The next loop iteration therefore parses bytes inside the ignored OBU as a new element while retaining an output cursor displaced by the complete ignored size. Packet growth accounts only for the newly parsed element, so its header or payload write begins beyond the allocated packet. A direct production-handler harness with a 100-byte temporal delimiter followed by 17 bytes produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow write 19 bytes beyond an 81-byte allocation on both sealed snapshots.
finding.code_snippet: if (obu_type == AV1_OBU_TEMPORAL_DELIMITER || obu_type == AV1_OBU_TILE_LIST) { pktpos += obu_size; rem_pkt_size -= obu_size; ... continue; }

vulnerability_trace.summary: discarding an ignored OBU advances only the logical output cursor and remaining length, so a following parser iteration grows a small packet and writes through a large unallocated gap

finding.description: Whisper allocates its audio queue from the queue duration, whose public minimum is 20 ms or 320 samples. It consumes complete upstream AVFrames without imposing a sample maximum. When one frame contains more samples than the queue, the capacity guard first transcribes at most the existing fill, then unconditionally copies the entire oversized frame into the fixed queue. FFmpeg's public asetnsamples filter can produce frames up to INT_MAX samples, establishing that no framework contract restricts an audio frame to the Whisper queue capacity. The sealed builds omit the optional Whisper dependency, so this remains source-confirmed rather than dynamically reproduced.

finding.description: RTP/LATM encodes an AAC access unit's size as one length byte per 255 payload bytes, but never ensures that this variable-length header fits the fixed RTP packet buffer before writing it. The public RTP muxer accepts AVPackets independently of the output packet size. With a normal 1,472-byte packet sink, a 382,500-byte AAC packet creates a 1,501-byte header; memset writes 1,500 bytes into the 1,472-byte allocation and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow on both sealed snapshots. The following fragmentation arithmetic would also become negative once the header exceeds max_payload_size.

finding.description: FFV1 level-4 remapping allocates each decoded lookup table for exactly slice_width times slice_height entries and records the number of populated entries, but entropy symbols are decoded in a ceil(log2(remap_count))-bit space. A valid 513x1 yuv444p16le remapped FFV1 packet has this shape. Flipping one entropy bit at packet byte 18 makes decode_line produce an out-of-range masked symbol, and decode_plane performs a two-byte heap-buffer-overflow read on both sealed snapshots.

finding.description: The common D3D12VA decoder allocates its fixed upload resource from the decoded frame's raw-image buffer size, but the H.264, HEVC, VC-1, VP9, and AV1 backends copy accepted compressed frame data into that mapped resource without checking the resulting byte count. Compressed-picture size is not bounded by decoded-image size. H.264 and HEVC additionally prepend three bytes per slice, VC-1 can prepend four-byte start codes, and AV1 can first accumulate partial tile groups into a separate heap buffer with the same raw-image-sized capacity before copying the unbounded total into the resource. The durable proof generates a standards-valid, normally decodable 16x5400 yuv420p H.264 Baseline stream whose slice bytes plus inserted prefixes exceed both the resource's 129,600-byte declared width and its 131,072-byte 64 KiB-aligned allocation floor. A valid 16x16 HEVC Main stream independently exceeds its 384-byte declared resource width. Later FFmpeg repairs add the missing capacity checks to the VC-1, VP9, and AV1 mapped copies and to AV1 accumulation, independently confirming those variants. The exact H.264 and HEVC byte counts are deterministically recorded by the proof script and can vary slightly with the installed encoder build. No Windows D3D12 runtime was available, so the root is retained as source-, producer-, and repair-confirmed rather than sanitizer-observed.

The do/while condition remains true forever, consuming one RTSP demuxing thread. finding.description: The public Icecast output protocol accepts stream metadata through string AVOptions and concatenates each nonempty value directly into its custom HTTP-header block. A value such as `safe-name\r\nX-Injected: yes` therefore terminates `Ice-Name` and creates a second attacker-chosen outbound header when the HTTP protocol appends that block verbatim. A loopback public `avio_open2` proof captures both headers from the pinned build. The identical proof against exact repair 99e1ecca36 captures neither header and logs its new CR/LF rejection. Scope requires an application to place untrusted data in an Icecast metadata option; ordinary media payload bytes do not control the value.
finding.code_snippet: if (NOT_EMPTY(value)) av_bprintf(bp, "%s: %s\r\n", key, value); ... av_dict_set(&opt_dict, "headers", headers, AV_DICT_DONT_STRDUP_VAL);
finding.poc: Build evaluations/ffmpeg_icecast_header_injection_reproducer.c against the pinned and repaired protocol-enabled FFmpeg trees, then run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_icecast_header_injection_reproducer.py to capture the two loopback HTTP requests.

vulnerability_trace.summary: an untrusted Icecast metadata value crosses a CRLF boundary into a verbatim outbound HTTP-header block

steps.note: A public encoding option supplies the stream-name string; applications that derive it from untrusted metadata expose the boundary.
The pinned build checks only that the value is nonempty and preserves embedded CR/LF bytes.
The crafted value becomes `Ice-Name: safe-name` followed by a new `X-Injected: yes` header line.
Icecast hands the complete poisoned header block to the HTTP protocol.
HTTP appends the custom block verbatim; the vulnerable loopback capture contains both the original and injected headers.
The exact later repair rejects metadata header values containing CR or LF and credits a security report.

finding.description: The public AV1 dovi_rpu bitstream filter assumes every successfully parsed Dolby Vision RPU produces replacement metadata. The parser deliberately returns success for an unrecognized RPU type, after which ff_dovi_get_metadata reports no metadata and update_rpu returns a NULL pointer with size zero. The AV1 path wraps that result in an AVBufferRef, changes the payload pointer to address 1, and assigns -1 to its unsigned payload size. CBS serialization then reads from address 1 while iterating the effectively unbounded payload. A public 56-byte AV1 metadata OBU deterministically aborts under ASan in cbs_av1_write_obu on the pinned build; exact repair 534f16d866 adds the missing no-RPU guard, and the identical packet is emitted cleanly.
finding.code_snippet: ref = av_buffer_create(rpu, rpu_size, av_buffer_default_free, NULL, 0); ... t35->payload = rpu + 1; t35->payload_size = rpu_size - 1;
finding.poc: Configure FFmpeg with --enable-bsf=dovi_rpu, build evaluations/ffmpeg_dovi_rpu_no_metadata_reproducer.c against the pinned and repaired ASan trees, then run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_dovi_rpu_no_metadata_reproducer.py to record the address-one crash/clean-output differential.

vulnerability_trace.summary: a valid AV1 Dolby metadata unit whose RPU parser returns success without metadata becomes a NULL/zero replacement, then pointer and size underflow make CBS serialize from address one

steps.note: The crafted public packet is a size-delimited AV1 ITU-T T.35 metadata OBU with the US country code and a sufficient payload.
Packet bytes select Dolby provider 0x003B and provider-oriented code 0x00000800, entering the RPU rewrite path.
The inner EMDF payload supplies RPU type zero, for which parsing intentionally succeeds without populating metadata.
The no-metadata state is explicitly represented to the caller as a successful NULL pointer and zero size.
The vulnerable caller accepts the NULL/zero result and creates a zero-sized buffer reference around it.
NULL plus one becomes address 1, while zero minus one becomes SIZE_MAX in the size_t payload field.
The CBS writer immediately reads from address 1; ASan reports the SEGV through cbs_av1_write_obu.
The exact later repair checks the missing postcondition before constructing the AV1 payload and identifies the issue as an out-of-array access.

finding.description: MVC2 stores its 128-entry RGB palette in an uninitialized stack array, initializes only the packet-declared number of colors, and later accepts seven-bit palette indices without checking them against that count. An eight-byte public decoder packet declares a 4x4 frame with zero colors and then selects palette index zero, copying four uninitialized stack bytes into all 16 returned RGB32 pixels. Compiling the vulnerable decoder source under deterministic pattern and zero automatic-variable initialization produces `pixel=aaaaaaaa` and `pixel=00000000` respectively through the identical public avcodec packet path, proving that stack contents cross into the decoded frame. A repair must reject every index greater than or equal to `nb_colors`; zero-initializing the array is only the differential proof.
finding.code_snippet: uint32_t color[128], v[8]; ... for (i = 0; i < FFMIN(nb_colors, 128); i++) color[i] = ...; ... set_4x4_block(..., color[p0 & 0x7F]);

vulnerability_trace.summary: an undeclared MVC2 palette index reads an uninitialized stack entry and publishes it as decoded RGB pixels

steps.note: The complete palette is automatic stack storage with no initializer.

No array entry is initialized when the declared palette is empty.
Packet bytes 00 80 select the equal-index palette-block form with index zero; the branch checks equality but not whether that index was declared.
The uninitialized four-byte palette entry is replicated into all 16 public output-frame pixels.
The normal public decoder callback returns the frame containing those stack-derived pixel bytes.

finding.description: VBLE forces YUV420P output and sizes its symbol buffer with FFmpeg's complete image-geometry helper, but it decodes both chroma planes with `width / 2` and `height / 2`. YUV420P instead uses ceiling subsampling for odd dimensions. A public 3x3 decoder proof supplies seventeen valid zero-length symbols and a `get_buffer2` callback that fills the codec-owned frame with 0xA5. The luma plane and first sample in each logical 2x2 chroma plane are decoded to zero, while the other six visible U/V samples remain 0xA5: `u=00a5/a5a5 v=00a5/a5a5`. The decoder therefore publishes prior buffer contents as visible chroma on odd-width or odd-height frames.
finding.code_snippet: int width_uv = avctx->width / 2, height_uv = avctx->height / 2; ... vble_restore_plane(ctx, pic, &gb, 1, offset, width_uv, height_uv); ... vble_restore_plane(ctx, pic, &gb, 2, offset, width_uv, height_uv);
finding.poc: Configure the pinned FFmpeg tree with --enable-decoder=vble, then build evaluations/ffmpeg_vble_odd_chroma_disclosure_reproducer.c through evaluations/run_ffmpeg_vble_odd_chroma_disclosure_reproducer.py to record the six visible marker bytes.

vulnerability_trace.summary: floor-divided 4:2:0 chroma geometry leaves visible samples unwritten and returns prior frame-buffer contents

steps.note: The decoder fixes output to a format whose chroma planes use ceiling-subsampled dimensions.
For 3x3 YUV420P the generic helper correctly counts nine luma plus two 2x2 chroma planes, or seventeen symbols.
The decoder incorrectly reduces each 3-pixel dimension to one rather than the required ceiling value two.
Only U[0,0] is written; the remaining three visible U samples preserve the marker.
The identical floor geometry leaves three visible V samples unwritten.
The public decoder returns the partially initialized frame without clearing or rejecting odd geometry.

finding.description: The S/PDIF probe checks for a seven-byte AAC ADTS header as though parsing started at the four-byte sync boundary, but spdif_get_offset_and_codec actually receives &buf[5]. A buffer ending after six logical ADTS bytes therefore passes the precondition and av_adts_header_parse consumes a seventh byte outside the declared buffer. This is reachable from WAV/W64 auto-detection, whose short-read buffer reserves padding but does not initialize it before ff_spdif_probe. The durable production-source proof passes a 14-byte logical buffer in a 15-byte allocation whose tail byte completes an ADTS header: the pinned probe sets codec=AAC, while exact repair 15bbf3a21d adds the missing byte to the bound and leaves the codec unset. The repair explicitly identifies an OSS-Fuzz read of uninitialized memory.
finding.code_snippet: if (buf + 4 + AV_AAC_ADTS_HEADER_SIZE > p_buf + buf_size) break; ... spdif_get_offset_and_codec(..., &buf[5], ...);
finding.poc: Build evaluations/ffmpeg_spdif_aac_probe_boundary_reproducer.c against the pinned static libraries and run evaluations/run_ffmpeg_spdif_aac_probe_boundary_reproducer.py with the exact repaired spdifdec.c source to record the codec=AAC versus codec=NONE boundary differential.

vulnerability_trace.summary: a one-byte-short S/PDIF AAC precondition lets the ADTS parser consume uninitialized storage beyond the logical probe buffer

steps.note: WAV/W64 codec auto-detection allocates padding but does not initialize bytes beyond a short read.
Only the number of bytes actually read is declared to the S/PDIF probe.
At the crafted sync position, this accepts exactly six logically available AAC header bytes because it is one byte short.
The AAC parser starts at byte five and requires seven bytes, consuming the byte immediately beyond the declared buffer.
The exact repair adds the missing byte and is explicitly tied to an OSS-Fuzz uninitialized-memory read.

finding.description: The D3D12 MPEG-2 accelerator allocates each upload resource at a fixed size derived from the decoded software-frame geometry, independently accumulates the compressed sizes of as many as 1,024 attacker-controlled slices, and copies that complete compressed bitstream into the mapped upload resource without comparing the two sizes. A sufficiently large validly framed MPEG-2 picture therefore writes past the GPU upload buffer from the CPU. Exact repair 26a9f9b3ae adds the missing ctx_pic->bitstream_size > ctx->bitstream_size guard immediately before mapping and copying. This remains source-confirmed because the current host has neither Windows nor a D3D12 decode device.
finding.code_snippet: ctx_pic->bitstream_size += size; ... memcpy(mapped_data, ctx_pic->bitstream, ctx_pic->bitstream_size);
finding.poc: On Windows with D3D12 MPEG-2 decode enabled, submit a picture whose accumulated slice payload exceeds ff_d3d12va_get_suitable_max_bitstream_size(); compare the pinned memcpy with exact repair 26a9f9b3ae, which rejects the frame before mapping the upload resource.

vulnerability_trace.summary: attacker-controlled MPEG-2 slice bytes can exceed the fixed D3D12 upload resource and are copied past its mapped boundary

steps.note: The upload capacity is derived from decoded frame geometry rather than the compressed packet length.
Every D3D12 upload resource is created at that fixed byte capacity.
Up to 1,024 externally supplied slice sizes are accumulated without a capacity comparison.
The complete compressed frame is copied to the smaller mapped resource, producing a CPU-side out-of-bounds write.
The exact later repair adds the absent size relation before the map and memcpy.

finding.description: When the public SCTP protocol is opened with max_streams, sctp_read reserves the first two output bytes for a stream ID but accepts read sizes zero or one. It passes buf+2 and size-2 to ff_sctp_recvmsg, so a one-byte read supplies a pointer beyond the caller's allocation and converts -1 to SIZE_MAX for recvmsg. Any received payload is written out of bounds; the following AV_WB16 also writes two stream-ID bytes into the one-byte caller buffer. Public direct AVIO reads can preserve such a caller-selected small size. Exact repair 5c3602abaa adds the size < 2 rejection already present in sctp_write. This remains source-confirmed because this macOS host lacks the SCTP kernel/API support needed for a faithful network reproduction.

finding.description: The PowerPC AltiVec vertical YUV-to-packed-RGB scaler is installed for RGB24/BGR24 and four 32-bit RGB layouts without requiring the destination width to be a multiple of sixteen. Its loop runs while i < dstW but every iteration emits a complete sixteen-pixel vector: 48 bytes for 24-bit output or 64 bytes for 32-bit output. The final iteration therefore writes past an exact-size destination row whenever dstW is not a multiple of sixteen. The apparent tail handler cannot contain the write because the loop exits with i >= dstW and its condition is `if (i < dstW)`. The public sws_scale API accepts caller-owned exact-size output buffers, so even a one-pixel destination can receive the full vector store. This remains source-confirmed because the current arm64 host cannot execute AltiVec code.
finding.code_snippet: for (i = 0; i < dstW; i += 16) { ... out_rgba(R, G, B, out); } if (i < dstW) { i -= 16; ... }
finding.poc: On a PowerPC host with AltiVec enabled but without a replacing VSX general-X implementation, use public sws_scale with a non-multiple-of-16 destination width, a general vertical filter, one of the installed RGB24/BGR24/ABGR/BGRA/ARGB/RGBA outputs, and an exact-size destination allocation; ASan should report the final 48- or 64-byte vector store beyond the row.

vulnerability_trace.summary: an unguarded non-multiple-of-sixteen destination reaches an AltiVec loop whose final iteration writes a complete packed-RGB vector beyond the public output buffer

steps.note: The normal AltiVec dispatch checks flags, alpha, and output format but imposes no destination-width alignment requirement.
The same assignment is made for six packed RGB layouts, making the vector routine the general vertical scaler.
The general public scaling path forwards the caller's output row and exact destination width unchanged.
Any positive remainder starts one final iteration even though fewer than sixteen output pixels remain.
The selected macro performs three 16-byte stores for 24-bit output or four for 32-bit output, overrunning an exact-size partial row.
After the loop, i is always greater than or equal to dstW, so the scratch-based partial handler is dead and cannot prevent the vector overrun.

finding.description: The IMF demuxer looks up a Chunk Path in attacker-controlled AssetMap XML and passes the result directly to xmlNodeGetContent without checking whether the element exists. A missing Path yields NULL, which is immediately passed to imf_uri_is_url and then strstr, causing a zero-page read and process abort. The ASan-enabled production ffprobe proof aborts in platform strstr on the minimal package, while exact repair 0fe4bd4b43 rejects the identical XML with 'missing Path element in Chunk'.
